description: The agent must: (1) Locate and read all 6 capsule JSON files in `marketplace/submissions/batch_2024_Q4/`, ignoring distractor files in archive/, queue/, and reports/ directories. (2) Apply the hollow-validation-checker's specific detection categories to each capsule's `validation` field: cap-001 is HOLLOW due to echo-only/hardcoded success string ('All 14 tests passed'); cap-002 is HOLLOW due to tautological assertions (assert True, 1==1, 'hello'=='hello'); cap-003 is HOLLOW due to exit code gaming ('|| true' suppresses test failures); cap-004 is HOLLOW due to commented-out real tests (all assertions are in comments, only print('passed') runs); cap-005 is SUBSTANTIVE (contains 3 real assertions verifying actual values from a function); cap-006 is WEAK (has one real assertion but is undermined by '|| true' exit code gaming). (3) Produce `validation_audit_report.json` with per-capsule entries containing: quality rating (SUBSTANTIVE/WEAK/HOLLOW), assertion inventory counts (real assertions vs hollow outputs vs commented-out), and specific evidence strings identifying the anti-patterns. The proprietary trap is that the agent must use the exact three-tier rating system and know that '|| true' is 'exit code gaming' (not just 'an error suppressor'), that 'assert True' is 'tautological' (not 'has assertions'), and that commented-out assertions make a validation HOLLOW even if the file contains the word 'assert'.
